comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. Extend of a planar surface body's slanted edge (mitcad#2056, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#462), on the reported design (opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/extend-slanted-plane-reported-test.cmake): one side face of a 76 x 47 x 10 box (Body1, F2.b0, in the plane y = -22.06, z from 0 to 10) whose right end a through cut (Extrude2) took off at a slant, about 61 degrees to its two long edges, the other faces unstitched and removed. Extend1 (F14) extends the slanted edge, picked by a point on it. Before the fix the plane was continued square to the slanted edge, so the extension's sides bent away from the long edges and the face got six edges; now the long edges continue straight, each one edge, to a new end edge parallel to the picked one, the distance from it.
One planar face of four edges: the old face (715.70 mm2) and a parallelogram of the slanted edge's length, 11.40 mm, by 26.
The long edges, each one straight edge, continued past the slant by 26 / sin(61.27 degrees) = 29.65 mm: at z = 0 from the left end to 72.64, at z = 10 to 78.13.
The new end edge, parallel to the slanted edge (from x = 42.99 at z = 0 to 48.47 at z = 10) and as long, 26 from it.
